applyTo: "**/*.spec,pyinstaller_hooks/**,etc/**,Makefile,src/Makefile,src/wiser/gui/Makefile,.github/workflows/**,install-win/**,install-linux/**,src/devtools/**,src/wiser/__main__.py"

# Packaging, platform, and dependencies

WISER ships as a frozen PyInstaller bundle to scientists on macOS (Intel and Apple
Silicon), Windows, and Linux. It is a **product, not a library** — "works on my machine
from source" is not evidence that a change works. Most defects in this area are invisible
in CI and surface only in the signed release, which is the most expensive place to find
them.

Treat platform compatibility as a P0 concern on any diff this file applies to.

## Frozen-build correctness

The bundle is not a source tree, and these differences bite repeatedly:

- **Imports must be discoverable statically.** PyInstaller traces imports; it cannot see
  `importlib.import_module`, `__import__`, a plugin loaded by name from config, or an
  optional dependency imported inside a function. A new dynamic import needs a
  `hiddenimports` entry in all three specs (`WISER.spec`, `WISER-macOS.spec`,
  `WISER-ubuntu.spec`) or it raises `ModuleNotFoundError` only in the release build.
  Check that a diff adding one updated **every** spec, not just the author's platform.
- **Data files must be declared.** Anything loaded by path — a `.json`, a lookup table,
  a colormap, a shader, a GDAL support file — needs a `datas` entry. A file that exists
  next to the module in the source tree does not exist in the bundle.
- **Paths differ under freeze.** `__file__`, `os.getcwd()`, and paths relative to the
  module are not what they are from source; bundled resources resolve under
  `sys._MEIPASS`. Flag new path construction that assumes a source layout.
- `src/tests`, `src/test_utils`, and `src/example_plugins` are **intentionally** included
  in the bundle so `--test_mode` can smoke-test the release. Do not suggest excluding
  them, and do not let a change break that self-test.
- `WISER_ENV` is forced to `prod` in frozen builds by
  `pyinstaller_hooks/set_wiser_env_prod.py`. Any feature gated below `prod` is invisible
  in the shipped product; check that a diff relying on a flag accounts for that.

## Cross-platform code

- **Process start method.** `fork` does not exist on Windows and is unsafe on macOS, so
  workers start via `spawn`. Code that relies on inherited state — a module-level object
  populated before the fork, an open file handle, an inherited GDAL dataset, a global
  set at import time — works on Linux and fails elsewhere. Everything the worker needs
  must be picklable and passed explicitly. This is the most common platform break in
  this codebase's architecture.
- **Paths.** Use `pathlib` or `os.path.join`; flag hardcoded `/` or `\`, `/tmp`,
  `~/Library`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%` outside the functions that deliberately branch on
  platform (`get_wiser_config_dir()` is the model — it branches explicitly).
- **Case sensitivity.** Linux filesystems are case-sensitive, macOS and Windows usually
  are not. A mismatched filename import or resource path passes locally and fails in CI
  or on a user's Linux box.
- **File locking and deletion.** Windows will not delete or rename a file that is still
  open. Cleanup code that works on POSIX can fail on Windows; check that handles close
  before the unlink, including on the error path.
- **Line endings and encoding.** ENVI headers and ASCII spectra are text files that come
  from all three platforms. Reading with the locale default encoding, or assuming `\n`,
  breaks on files a collaborator produced elsewhere. Specify the encoding.
- **Apple Silicon versus Intel.** Both are shipped. Flag anything that assumes x86 —
  architecture-specific binaries, AVX intrinsics, a wheel with no `osx-arm64` build.
  `check_arch.sh` exists because mixed-architecture bundles have shipped before.
- `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0` sets the oldest supported macOS. A dependency or API
  requiring newer raises the floor for every user; call it out.
- Qt itself differs across platforms in DPI handling, default fonts, menu placement
  (macOS moves items into the application menu), and native dialogs. A layout tuned to
  one platform's metrics is worth a comment.

## Dependencies

The environment is conda-locked, not pip-resolved. A new dependency is a bigger
commitment here than in a typical Python project:

- Sources live in `etc/wiser-prod.yml` and `etc/wiser-dev-additions.txt`;
  `etc/wiser-dev.yml` is **generated** from those by `make_dev_env.py`, and
  `prod-conda-lock.yml` / `dev-conda-lock.yml` are generated by `conda-lock`. Flag a
  hand-edited generated file, and flag a source change with no regenerated lockfile —
  CI restores the environment from the lock, so the dependency will not be there.
- Lockfiles must resolve for **all five platforms**: `linux-64`, `linux-aarch64`,
  `osx-64`, `osx-arm64`, `win-64`. A package without builds for all of them cannot be
  added as-is.
- Runtime dependencies also increase installer size and code-signing surface. A large
  dependency added for one utility function deserves a question.
- Check license compatibility. WISER is open source with copyright held jointly by
  Caltech and the Regents of the University of Colorado; a copyleft runtime dependency
  in a distributed binary is a legal question, not a preference.
- Distinguish dev-only from runtime: a test or tooling dependency belongs in
  `wiser-dev-additions.txt`, not in the prod environment that ships.
- Pin deliberately. A floating version in a product that is signed and notarized means
  two builds of the same tag can differ.

## Build, CI, and generated artifacts

- **Python is 3.12** (`etc/wiser-dev.yml`). Note that `pyproject.toml` sets ruff's
  `target-version = "py39"` and the lint job installs ruff under Python 3.9 — that is
  the linter's configuration, not the runtime. Do not tell contributors to write 3.9
  code, and do not flag 3.10+ syntax on those grounds.
- Ruff is pinned to `0.1.15` in CI. A diff that reformats under a different ruff version
  will fail `ruff format --check`; if a diff bumps the pin, expect repo-wide churn and
  say so.
- `.ui` and `.qrc` sources require `make generated`, and the target list is enumerated by
  hand in `src/wiser/gui/Makefile` (`FILENAMES`) and `src/Makefile` (`TARGETS`). A new
  `.ui` file without its `Makefile` entry is simply never built — the import fails for
  everyone who runs `make generated` on a clean tree. Check for the pairing.
- Generated output under `src/wiser/gui/generated/` is not reviewed and should not be
  hand-edited.
- Signing and notarization (`src/devtools/sign_mac.py`, `sign_windows.py`, the NSIS
  installer) are release machinery. Credentials come from `Secret.sh` / `Secret.mk` or
  the environment and must never reach process arguments, logs, or the repository —
  flag any diff that passes a secret on a command line or echoes one.
- A change to build or packaging is not verified by the unit suite. The real check is
  `make smoke-test-mac-build` / `smoke-test-win-build` (`--test_mode` against the frozen
  bundle) on the affected platforms. Say plainly when a diff needs that and CI cannot
  provide it.
